children.label: Overview
children: Observation: skin color, chest movement during ventilation
Equipment monitoring
Qualified anesthesia personnel present throughout
HR and BP measured every 5 min, drugs and fluids charted
Oxygenation, ventilation, circulation and temperature continually evaluated

children.label: Normal values under anesthesia
children: SBP 85-160, DBP 50-95 mmHg
SpO2 95-100%, ETCO2 33-45 mmHg
Temperature 36-37.5 °C
Urine output 0.5 ml/kg/min or more (as written in the lecture)
CVP 1-10 mmHg, MAP 80-120 mmHg
MAP = DBP + 1/3 (SBP - DBP)

children.label: Depth of anesthesia
children: BIS 40-60: recommended for general anesthesia
BIS below 40: deep; above 60: may be conscious; 60-90 sedation; 100 awake
Inadequate: grimacing, movement; if paralyzed, hypertension, tachycardia, tearing, sweating
Excessive: bradycardia, hypotension, cardiac depression
BIS may reduce intraoperative awareness

children.label: ECG
children: 3 leads usually (lead II), 5 leads for complicated patients
5-lead system adds V5 and limb leads
ST depression = ischemia, elevation = infarction
Over 85% of ischemic events seen in leads II and V5
P wave in lead II helps identify sinus rhythm

children.label: Pulse oximetry
children: Measures Hb saturation (normal above 90%, usually 97-98%)
Red and infrared light absorption difference between oxyHb and deoxyHb
CO poisoning gives falsely high reading
Inaccurate with poor perfusion, vasoconstriction, movement, dysrhythmia, cautery interference, methylene blue

children.label: Blood pressure
children: Palpation (SBP only), Korotkoff auscultation, automated non-invasive, invasive arterial
Automated cuff measures every ~5 min and may stop reading in sudden severe hypotension
Invasive indications: rapid BP changes, frequent sampling, major surgery, vasoactive drugs
Also burns, morbid obesity, severe metabolic abnormality, major trauma
Radial artery is the most common site; femoral, brachial, dorsalis pedis alternatives

children.label: Central venous pressure
children: Line in internal jugular, subclavian or femoral vein reaching SVC or IVC
Reflects RA and RV pressure, intravascular volume, RV preload
Measure at end-expiration, trends more useful than single values
Not needed for minor surgery
Right internal jugular: predictable landmarks, straight course, 90-99% success
Complications: infection, bleeding, air embolism, pneumothorax, carotid puncture, arrhythmia
Chest X-ray after upper-body insertion; ultrasound guidance helps

children.label: Capnography and ETCO2
children: Capnometry = number, capnogram = waveform, capnography = continuous monitoring
Under GA keep ETCO2 about 32-35, not below 30 (cerebral vasoconstriction)
PaCO2 minus ETCO2 about 5 mmHg
Best method to confirm intubation and extubation
Also adequacy of ventilation, PE, partial obstruction, bronchospasm, resuscitation outcome
Increased: hyperthermia, sepsis, thyroid storm, MH, hypoventilation, rebreathing, laparoscopy
Decreased: hypothermia, hyperventilation, hypoperfusion, embolism
Waveform: phase I dead space, II upstroke, III alveolar plateau, IV downstroke

children.label: Cyanosis
children: Defined as 5 g/dL deoxygenated hemoglobin
Normal Hb 15: SaO2 66%, PaO2 35 mmHg
Anemic Hb 10: SaO2 50%, PaO2 27 mmHg
In anemia, cyanosis appears at a lower oxygen tension

children.label: Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve
children: Sigmoid curve of PaO2 against saturation
Below PaO2 60 (SpO2 90%) saturation falls rapidly; lowest acceptable SpO2 is 90%
Left shift: alkalosis, low 2,3-DPG, hypothermia, low CO2, fetal Hb, COHb, methemoglobin; higher affinity
Right shift: acidosis, high CO2, hyperthermia, high 2,3-DPG, altitude, sickle cell, inhalational agents; lower affinity
Right shift releases O2 to tissues more easily
O2 content = binding capacity x saturation + dissolved O2

children.label: Temperature and urine output
children: Keep theatre at 22 °C or higher
Heat loss under anesthesia 0.5-1 °C per hour; below 34 °C significant morbidity
High risk: elderly, burns, neonates, spinal cord injury
Hyperthermia causes: MH, pyrogens, overwarming, thyrotoxicosis, pheochromocytoma
Sites: tympanic, esophagus, rectum, nasopharynx
Foley catheter in major surgery; below 0.5 ml/kg/min is oliguria
Choose monitors by surgery size (no CVP, arterial line or BIS for appendectomy)
